ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Measures for the Administration of Beneficial Owner Information of Legal Entities and Other Organizations (PBOC/SAMR Order No. 3, effective November 1, 2024); Anti-Money Laundering Law of the People's Republic of China (2024 Amendment, effective January 1, 2025); Measures for Anti-Money Laundering and Anti-Terrorist Financing of Financial Institutions (PBOC, 2016); Regulations of the People's Republic of China on the Administration of Registration of Market Entities (State Council Order No. 746); Company Law of the People's Republic of China (2023 Revision).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent corporate registry in the foreign investor's jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille sequence only if the origin jurisdiction is an Apostille Convention member: notarize the certificate, obtain an Apostille from the designated competent authority, then produce a certified Chinese translation. Consular Legalization sequence only if the origin jurisdiction is a non-member: notarize the certificate, authenticate it before the local foreign affairs or justice ministry, then legalize it at the Chinese Embassy or Consulate, and produce a certified Chinese translation. Apostille and consular legalization are parallel alternatives and must never be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registry of companies or commercial registrar of the foreign investor's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille sequence only for Apostille Convention member states: notary certification, Apostille by the competent authority, certified Chinese translation. Consular Legalization sequence only for non-member states: notary certification, local ministry authentication, Chinese consular legalization, certified Chinese translation. The two authentication paths are mutually exclusive and parallel; never apply consular legalization to an already apostilled document.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors or shareholders of the foreign corporate investor, certified by a notary public in the jurisdiction of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: If the document originates in a Hague Apostille Convention state: notarize the executed resolution or power of attorney, then obtain an Apostille from the designated competent authority, followed by certified Chinese translation. If the document originates in a non-member state: notarize, authenticate through the local competent authority, obtain consular legalization from the Chinese Embassy or Consulate, then translate into certified Chinese. The routes are alternative, not sequential.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (Memorandum and Articles / Charter)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry or duly authorized company secretary of the foreign investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path for Apostille Convention countries: notarize the articles, affix an Apostille from the designated local competent authority, and proceed to certified Chinese translation. Consular Legalization path for non-Apostille countries: notarize the articles, obtain local foreign-affairs authentication, secure Chinese consular legalization, and proceed to certified Chinese translation. Do not chain the two methods; only one path applies based on the origin state's membership in the Apostille Convention.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Investor's relationship bank or qualifying financial institution maintaining the corporate accounts
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For a bank reference letter issued in an Apostille Convention member state: have the issuing bank sign before a notary, obtain an Apostille from the competent authority, and translate into certified Chinese. For a bank reference letter issued in a non-member state: notarize the banker's signature and corporate authority, authenticate through the local competent ministry, legalize at the Chinese Embassy or Consulate, and translate into certified Chinese. Apostille and consular legalization are mutually exclusive alternatives.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening is performed against the UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list, OFAC SDN list, EU consolidated sanctions list, China's domestic terrorist and designated entities lists, and globally published regulatory enforcement actions. UBOs, directors, signatories and beneficiaries are screened for PEP status using commercial AML databases, adverse media, corporate registry beneficial-ownership data, and China's PBOC beneficial-owner filing system. Enhanced due diligence requires re-verification every 180 days for high-risk PEPs, source-of-funds documents, transaction rationale, and escalation to the AML compliance officer. All screening results are timestamped and retained for at least five years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: SAMR National Enterprise Registration Online Service Platform (Enterprise Name Online Reservation system), accessed through provincial market regulation administration portals
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Statutory naming requires the registered name to be in simplified Chinese characters, composed strictly of four tiers in the following order: administrative division, distinctive name, industry or operating characteristic, and enterprise form. The distinctive segment must contain at least two Chinese characters and must not be identical to, or confusingly similar to, an existing enterprise name or registered trademark in the same industry. Latin letters, Arabic numerals, and pinyin transliteration are not permitted in the registered Chinese name, except where a special foreign-invested enterprise rule allows a parenthetical foreign name or industry token; a separate English trade name may be used commercially but must be disclosed to banks, customs and tax authorities and kept documentary-consistent with the Chinese legal name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: An applicant may immediately re-submit a revised Chinese company name through the SAMR online name reservation platform upon rejection. To contest an adverse determination, the applicant must file a written administrative reconsideration request with the provincial market regulation bureau within 60 days after receiving the rejection notice, setting out the legal basis, the proposed four-tier name structure, and search evidence showing no identical or confusingly similar existing name. If reconsideration is denied or not decided, administrative litigation may be brought before the competent People's Court within six months. Preserve rejection screenshots, submission numbers, correspondence and all supporting trademark or registry reports.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office and commercial mailbox arrangements are impermissible for a WFOE engaged in OOG or heavy-haul project cargo logistics. The registered address must be a physical, surveyed office or industrial premises that is leased in the WFOE name and used for operational management, contract negotiation, documentation, and customs-related records. Tax authorities reject a virtual-only address because no actual business substance exists; banks reject it for account opening and may freeze an account if address inconsistency is discovered. In selected pilot free-trade zones, a registered address service may be used only when combined with a separate actual operating site in the zone for logistics activities. PO Boxes are never acceptable.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Probability of unannounced inspection within the first 24 months is high, estimated at 65-75% for WFOEs in ISIC 5229 (project cargo logistics) with VAT rebate or customs activity. Municipal tax authorities and SAMR may inspect without notice to verify that the registered office is not a mailbox. Inspection checklist: name plate at the door; lease or ownership certificate; utility bills in the company name; staff presence and attendance records; statutory books and seals; corporate bank statements; freight forwarding agreements; customs and import-export records. Failure to satisfy these indicators triggers penalties, blacklisting, revocation risk and bank account restrictions.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official fee waived; no government charge for name clearance or incorporation under the current national fee schedule.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Unified Social Credit Code and business license issuance
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official fee nil; issuance is included in the free market entity registration procedure.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: No statutory fee for automatic tax registration or seal filing at WFOE establishment.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization and authentication of foreign investor document bundle (five required instruments)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Foreign notary public, competent apostille authority, or Chinese Embassy or Consulate for consular legalization
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official notary, apostille and consular fee schedule plus market handling fee; varies by foreign jurisdiction.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Qualified translation agency or PRC law firm
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market translation tariff per page or word; standard five-document WFOE bundle.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Company seal set (official, financial, contract and customs seals)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for four seals in major PRC registration cities.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office lease due diligence and virtual-office risk assessment
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed market fee for lease review, address substance memo, and bank or tax acceptance analysis.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: External PRC legal counsel incorporation retainer
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing fixed retainer for WFOE setup including Chinese name selection, articles, capital registration and post-incorporation filings.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/KYC/UBO disclosure, PEP and sanctions screening close-out package
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: AML compliance service provider or PRC law firm

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Company Law of the People's Republic of China (2023 Revision), Articles 1-5, 7, 23-39, 40-56, 57-85, 89-93, 100, 127; Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (2020), Articles 4-6, 10, 31; Regulations for the Implementation of the Foreign Investment Law (2020), Articles 2-6, 18-20; Civil Code of the People's Republic of China, Articles 58-75
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) through the local Municipal Market Supervision Administration and the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System (NECIPS)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Foreign-Invested Company Establishment Registration Application Form, Foreign Investment Information Report, and Unified Social Credit Code Application
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum registered capital is prescribed for a WFOE limited liability company under PRC law, and no blocked escrow is required; however, each shareholder must fully pay the subscribed capital within the period set in the Articles of Association, and funds introduced from abroad must be registered with the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) and deposited into a designated capital settlement account before external use
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that this Board of Directors of [Company Name] WFOE Limited Liability Company ('the Company'), holding a validly constituted meeting on the ___ day of __________, 20___, with the directors present in person and by proxy, and acting pursuant to the Company Law of the People's Republic of China and the Articles of Association: 1. Share Capital Subscription. The board hereby approves the issuance and subscription of the registered capital of CNY ______, divided into ______ ordinary shares, subscribed by the shareholders as set out in the capital contribution schedule attached hereto. Each shareholder shall transmit the full stated contribution from their overseas or domestic legal source into the Company's designated foreign capital settlement account no later than the date fixed in the Articles of Association. The board confirms that no share may be issued at below par value, that no set-off shall be recognized except as specifically approved in writing, and that a capital verification report shall be obtained if required by the Foreign Investment Information System or by a licensed bank. 2. Banking Authorization. The board designates the Company's basic deposit account and its foreign exchange capital account to be opened with such commercial bank in Shanghai as nominated by the General Manager. The Legal Representative, together with the General Manager and any one officer designated in the appended signatory schedule, are jointly and severally authorized to sign account-opening forms, funds transfer instructions, and foreign exchange purchase/settlement documents, subject to the dual-signature limit of CNY ______. 3. Registered Office Adoption. The board adopts the premises located at _______________, City District, Shanghai, China, as the statutory registered office and legal seat of the Company, and confirms that the lease certificate, ownership certificate, or notarized rental agreement has been inspected and will be retained at the company's file register for submission to the SAMR registration authority. 4. Appointments. The board appoints ______ as Chairman of the Board and Legal Representative; ______ as General Manager; ______ as Chief Financial Officer; and ______ as a Statutory Supervisor. The Legal Representative and General Manager are each authorized to execute the incorporation application, foreign investment information report, and any lease, employment, tax registration, and bank documentation necessary to bring the Company fully into operation. 5. General Powers. The board resolves that the Company may carry on the business of out-of-gauge project-cargo logistics, including freight forwarding, road and water hauling, customs coordination, heavy-lift crane coordination, and ancillary services, and that all external filings shall be made in strict compliance with the Foreign Investment Law and the Company Law. The resolution is effective immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Reservation and Negative List Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: SAMR Enterprise Registration Portal through the local Municipal Market Supervision Administration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The foreign shareholders select three to five unique proposed company names and submit them via the unified enterprise registration portal together with the proposed business scope covering ISIC 5229 out-of-gauge project-cargo logistics. The system checks name conflicts, prohibited words, and the foreign investment negative list. The legal representative or designated agent must upload the notarized passport or apostilled identity certificate of each shareholder, a draft Articles of Association, and a letter of intent or lease for the future registered office. Once the name is approved, a Name Reservation Notice is issued and remains valid for six months; any rejection due to negative-list restriction or name similarity may be cured by amending the business scope or selecting an alternative name.
required_dossiers: Completed Name Reservation Application
Scanned passport or notarized identity document of each foreign shareholder
Foreign investor notarial certificate or apostille
Lease intent letter or preliminary property lease
Proposed Articles of Association draft
Signed list of proposed business scope in English and Chinese
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried due to name conflict, negative-list restriction, or insufficient translation, amend the proposed legal name and business scope, re-submit the name reservation, or provide a bilingual conformity explanation; a rejected reservation may be resubmitted immediately after correction.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: WFOE Incorporation Filing with SAMR and Issuance of Business License
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the approved Name Reservation Notice, the applicant submits the final signed Articles of Association, the Foreign Investment Information Report, board appointment resolutions, the passport or ID of the legal representative, the notarized or apostilled foreign shareholder documents, and proof of the registered office address through the SAMR local one-stop enterprise registration portal. The authority reviews the capital structure, business scope, lease legality, and foreign investment negative-list compliance. Upon approval, the company is assigned a Unified Social Credit Code and issued the official WFOE Business License. The business license is the foundation for all subsequent banking, tax, customs, and industry permit procedures.
required_dossiers: Name Reservation Notice
Signed Articles of Association in English and Chinese versions
Foreign Investment Information Report
Notarized board appointment resolutions and legal representative identification
Property ownership certificate or registered lease agreement for the registered office
Feasibility description of the project-cargo heavy-haul operation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SAMR issues a correction notice, revise the business scope to exclude restricted categories, upload the missing lease or ownership certificate, or amend the Articles of Association within 30 days; if the location fails legal address requirements, select a different registerable premises and refile.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Seal Engraving, Bank Account Opening, and SAFE Foreign Exchange Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Security Bureau authorized seal engraving firm, licensed commercial bank, and State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the business license is obtained, the WFOE must engrave the company seal, legal representative seal, finance seal, and contract seal through an engraving firm authorized by the Public Security Bureau, and record the seal imprints in the public security filing system. The legal representative then opens the company basic deposit account and the foreign exchange capital account at a board-approved licensed bank, and files the foreign investment capital registration through the SAFE digital foreign exchange system within 30 days of establishment. All foreign capital contributions are credited to the capital settlement account, and the bank monitors the declared purpose and payment schedule. The board resolution executed in the formation file must be presented as the signatory authority support.
required_dossiers: Original WFOE business license
Unified Social Credit Code certificate
Legal representative passport and negligible-board authorization
Articles of Association and the pro-forma first board resolution
Seal imprint certificate from the engraving firm
Board appointment letter for authorized account signatories
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank rejects account opening due to enhanced due diligence, supply beneficial-ownership declarations, a referral letter from an existing partner bank, or choose another licensed bank; for SAFE rejection, correct the capital payment schedule and shareholder commitment records and resubmit through the portal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, Statistical, and Social Insurance Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) local tax service office, National Bureau of Statistics, and Municipal Social Insurance Authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The WFOE must complete tax registration after the business license is granted, obtaining a taxpayer identification number and registering for corporate income tax, value-added tax, stamp duty, urban maintenance and construction tax, and education surcharge. For logistics services with project-cargo milestones, the company must also file a general VAT taxpayer application if annual revenue is expected to exceed the statutory threshold, or maintain small-scale taxpayer status otherwise simultaneously, the company must complete survey and statistical registration with the local statistics bureau and register its employees with the municipal social insurance and housing fund system. All activities are centralized on the integrated online service platform, and failure to register within 30 days triggers a late-registration warning and possible administrative penalty.
required_dossiers: Business license copy and Unified Social Credit Code
Articles of Association and first board resolution
Legal representative identification and tax payment agreement
Lease certificate and project contracts for logistics services
Employee roster, social insurance registration forms, and housing provident fund data
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If tax or social insurance registration is delayed, submit a written explanation with the relevant business license and lease documents to the local STA and social insurance office, pay any minimal administrative warning, and ask for restoration of the tax account before invoicing operations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Transport Operating Permit and Out-of-Gauge Route Clearance Licensing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Provincial or Municipal Transportation Bureau under the Ministry of Transport, and the Highway Administration for over-limit route permits
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: For third-party project-cargo heavy-haul operations on public roads, the WFOE must apply for a Road Freight Operating Permit covering general freight transport, or alternatively file a freight-forwarding coordination service registration if all carriage is performed by licensed subcontractors. The application must include the proposed fleet list, driver qualifications, vehicle registrations, and the emergency response plan. For each dimensionally over-limit or overweight movement, a separate Out-of-Gauge Transport Route Permit must be obtained from the highway administrator, accompanied by route surveys, bridge load calculations, police escort plans, and cargo securing drawings. If the company owns fixed staging yards or repair sheds, municipal structural and fire safety approvals are mandatory before operation.
required_dossiers: WFOE business license and Unified Social Credit Code
Road Freight Operating Permit application form
Vehicle registration and driver qualification documents or executed subcontractor contracts
Out-of-gauge cargo transport plan, route map, and axle-load calculation for each movement
Cargo/third-party liability insurance certificates
Bridge and road engineering clearance reports for overweight moves
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the transport or route permit is refused, recalculate axle loads and secured dimensions, submit a revised route using a stronger bridge or alternate corridor, provide a bank guarantee for bridge protection, and file an administrative reconsideration with the provincial transport commission within 60 days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Transport (MOT) through the provincial or municipal Transportation Bureau; SAMR for market-access registration; Municipal Fire and Rescue Department for fire-safety clearance
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Road Freight Transport Operating Permit, Out-of-Gauge Cargo Transport Route Permit, and, for any operated staging yard or maintenance shed, a Fire Safety Inspection Certificate

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Ecology and Environment (MEE) of the People's Republic of China and the provincial or municipal Ecology and Environment Bureau
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Environmental Registration (EIA Filing) under the Classified Administration List of Construction Projects for Environmental Impact Assessment; the WFOE is treated as a logistics-support service with no production line, so a full EIA Report is not required unless the project includes permanent diesel storage above one cubic meter, a vehicle washing or painting bay, or hazardous waste storage exceeding ten tons per year, in which case a Category B EIA Report is required
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Domestic sewage must comply with GB 18918-2002 Grade B before municipal discharge; vehicle washing wastewater must pass oil separation and meet COD not exceeding 100 mg/L and petroleum oil not exceeding 5 mg/L; diesel vehicles must meet China VI emission limits; volatile organic compound emissions from any painting operation must not exceed 60 mg/Nm3; hazardous waste such as used lubricants, batteries, and filters must be stored in compliance with GB 18597-2023 and transported to a licensed hazardous-waste disposal operator within 180 days

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Inspection Certificate for the registered office, repair sheds, and any staging yard with structures exceeding 300 square meters; structural safety review and civil-defense clearance for loading platforms and temporary storage areas; registration and annual inspection of forklifts, cranes, and hoisting equipment under the Special Equipment Safety Law; occupational health and safety production facilities approved under the Production Safety Law of the People's Republic of China

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration of the People's Republic of China (STA), administered through provincial and municipal Tax Service Bureaus and the unified Electronic Tax Service Platform (state-level portal: etax.chinatax.gov.cn)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise (WFOE): first obtain the Chinese Unified Social Credit Code (USCC) as the legal entity identifier from the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) business registration; then complete tax registration with the STA within 30 days of issuance of the business license through the Electronic Tax Service Platform. The WFOE must file the standard tax registration dataset, including the approved business license, articles of association, lease or ownership proof of the registered office, legal representative identity documents, capitalization and financial contribution schedule, bank account opening certificate for the basic deposit account, and, where applicable, foreign investment negative-list screening results. The USCC functions as the taxpayer identification number; the STA separately assigns a VAT registration detail code. A non-resident foreign enterprise without a Chinese business establishment may be issued a non-resident tax registration ID for withholding tax administration; however, the CN_WFOE_LTD is a Chinese resident enterprise and is registered on the national taxpayer file directly.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. China does not provide check-the-box entity classification elections for domestic limited liability companies. A WFOE is automatically a Chinese tax resident enterprise subject to Enterprise Income Tax (EIT) on worldwide income. The only classification election relevant to this entity is the VAT general taxpayer versus small-scale taxpayer status election; no hybrid-mismatch check-the-box election is available under Chinese domestic law.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Value-Added Tax) under the Notice on Comprehensively Advancing the Pilot Program of Replacing Business Tax with Value-Added Tax (Caishui [2016] No. 36), the Provisional Regulations on VAT, and the associated implementing rules on VAT in the People's Republic of China
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: All WFOEs must register for VAT from entity creation; the mandatory general taxpayer registration threshold is annual taxable turnover in excess of RMB 5,000,000 within any continuous 12-month period. A taxpayer below the threshold may elect small-scale VAT status, under which the simplified VAT rate is generally 3% (with 5% applicable to certain property leasing and real estate transactions). Once the RMB 5,000,000 threshold is exceeded, small-scale status is lost and the entity must operate as a general taxpayer; logistics auxiliary and freight-forwarding services are then taxable at the 6% modern-services rate, while transport services supplied as actual carrier are taxable at 9% and sales of tangible goods at 13%.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: China has fully implemented the fully digitalized electronic invoice (Digitalized Special VAT Invoice) regime through the STA Electronic Tax Service Platform. All VAT invoices must be issued via the official e-invoice system and must carry the STA-assigned unique invoice number and cryptographic anti-fraud check code; no invoice is valid for input VAT deduction unless it has passed through this mandatory fiscal clearance. The Golden Tax IV digital tax control system performs real-time transmission, reconciliation, and anti-fraud verification of invoice data against customs declarations, bank foreign-exchange records, and enterprise reporting data. Business ERP or billing systems must integrate through STA-approved invoicing APIs; failure to issue through the approved e-invoice pipeline can invalidate deduction rights and attract administrative penalties.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: For physical goods exported from China, the vendor is eligible for VAT zero-rating and the export tax refund mechanism (exemption, credit, and refund) when the goods are actually shipped out of China through a customs-supervised port and the export customs declaration is completed by the export seller. For cross-border services, the STA applies zero-rating to qualifying international transportation services supplied by the carrier; logistics auxiliary services such as freight forwarding, warehousing, cargo handling, and out-of-gauge heavy-haul project logistics are VAT-exempt rather than zero-rated when the service is supplied to an overseas enterprise or to an international transportation operation and the consideration is received through the foreign-exchange and customs control environment. The CN_WFOE_LTD must substantiate that the underlying project cargo was physically exported from China, that the logistics service was contractually ordered by a non-resident shipping principal or consignee, and that no taxable materialization of the service remained inside China's VAT jurisdiction.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Goods Declaration Form (electronic customs export declaration with the 19-digit customs declaration reference number)
Bill of Lading or Sea Waybill (for ocean heavy-haul project cargo) / Master Air Waybill or international consignment note (for air or cross-border road transport)
Packing List and out-of-gauge heavy-lift cargo manifest with container, unit dimensions, and weight certificates
Commercial Invoice issued to the overseas buyer, consignee, or non-resident shipping principal

Export foreign-exchange collection declaration and bank foreign-exchange receipt voucher evidencing inward remittance under the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) trade-in-trade monitoring system
Bank settlement voucher or letter-of-credit advice evidencing the receipt of export proceeds
Export tax rebate declaration package transmitted through the STA export-tax-rebate electronic system, with customs release data reconciled to the VAT invoice amount and service contract
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The STA, the General Administration of Customs, and the SAFE maintain a joint data intelligence framework that cross-checks customs export declarations, VAT invoice issuance, logistics documentation, and foreign-exchange receipts. Where export zero-rating or VAT exemption is disallowed on audit, the STA claws back the VAT exemption, refund, or credit amount, imposes late-payment interest, and may assess a penalty of 50% to 500% of the underpaid tax under the Law on the Administration of Tax Levying where false declaration or tax evasion is established. False export declarations also trigger penalties under the Customs Law, ranging from 50% to 300% of the customs value, suspension of import/export registration, and cancellation of export-tax-rebate status. Criminal liability is available under Article 204 of the Criminal Law for fraudulent export tax refunds, with imprisonment and fines available against the WFOE and its responsible management.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBOC) and the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE), which exercises delegated FX administration powers
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: China operates a managed floating exchange rate regime with RMB fully convertible on the current account (trade in goods/services, dividends, and wages) under Article VIII of the IMF Articles of Agreement, while the capital account remains heavily regulated and dependent on SAFE approvals or filings. The Foreign Investment Law and the 2020 Regulations on Foreign Exchange Control (State Council Decree No. 532) guarantee that profits and dividends of WFOEs can be remitted offshore after tax audits and statutory audit certificates, subject to bank verification of prior-year audited financials and tax payment proofs. Capital account items, including foreign direct investment down payments, intercompany loans, and returns on equity, require registration with SAFE through the bank-based Foreign Exchange Registration System (FDI system) and face a negative-list screening. Surrender requirements for export proceeds have been abolished; exporters may hold foreign currency in domestic or offshore accounts, but every receipt must be reported under the International Balance of Payments (BOP) statistics with genuine trade documentation. Renminbi can be used for cross-border settlement under the CIPS mechanism, reducing direct FX exposure for certain transactions, but a substantial portion of project cargo contracts remains USD-denominated, necessitating a comprehensive treasury hedging plan.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the People's Bank of China/SAFE 2020 Guidance on Foreign Exchange Operations for Current Account Items, there is no statutory mandatory surrender ratio or timeline for export foreign currency receipts. Enterprises are permitted to retain 100% of export proceeds abroad or in domestic designated foreign exchange settlement accounts. However, all inward receipts must be declared to the BOP through the bank within 30 days of collection (via the Merchant Foreign Exchange Payment and Receipt Declaration system). The bank will conduct 'genuine transaction' verification against the customs declaration, contract, invoice, and logistics documents. If the export proceeds are not repatriated within a reasonable business cycle, SAFE may require an explanation and could add the entity to its monitoring list. For imports, payment in foreign currency requires a corresponding import customs declaration or other trade documents.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Foreign Exchange Capital Account (FDI Capital Escrow)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Basic Deposit Account and Foreign Exchange Settlement Account
Basic Deposit Account with CNY and FX settlement functions
Basic Deposit Account with export settlement function

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Not viable as a primary acquiring/payment rail for a mainland WFOE. Under the PRC Payment and Settlement Regulations, non-bank financial institutions must obtain a payment license from PBOC to provide online payment services; as of the current regulatory landscape, offshore digital EMI institutions (e.g., Revolut, Wise, Airwallex) are not licensed to open or maintain domestic foreign currency accounts for Chinese resident entities. They can only serve as ancillary remittance aggregators in some cross-border e-commerce pilots, but the WFOE's capital account controls, FX settlement, and profit repatriation must be executed through domestically licensed banks. Any attempt to route investment proceeds or trade payments through unlicensed EMIs would violate SAFE circulars on the 'capability of cross-border receiving and payment' and risk account freezing, fines, and adverse compliance findings. Therefore, the blueprint should integrate with domestic Tier-1 banks for FX and clearing, while using reputable global cash management banks for offshore salary/benefit payments if needed.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical in-branch appearance of the statutory legal representative (or the manager with a board resolution and a notarized power of attorney) is mandatory for opening a basic deposit account and the related capital/fx accounts under the PBOC's Account Opening Administrative Rules. Remote consular proxy opening is generally NOT permitted for WFOE accounts, although some banks may accept a video interview combined with a notarized Chinese-language authorization executed at the Chinese embassy/consulate in the shareholder's home country for the initial account setup documentation. The first meeting, however, must occur in the physical branch of the chosen bank, and the account activation (with payment limits) typically requires submission of original company chops (seals). This is a non-waivable KYC requirement under the PBOC 2016 No.1 Circular on anti-money laundering.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) chain involving offshore jurisdictions and nominee shareholders with no transparent economic substance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified corporate registration certificates (Certificate of Incorporation, Articles of Association), a full shareholding chain up to the ultimate individual(s) with passport copies, a confirmation of no nominee shareholding from the registered agent, and a UBO declaration form on the bank's format. For any offshore holding company, provide the annual return, a certificate of good standing, and audited financial statements for the last two years.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-based money laundering anomaly: the declared project cargo logistics scope appears inconsistent with high-value freight payments, e.g., servicing fees versus physical transport costs.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Original signed project cargo contracts (heavy lift and OOG), the specific shipping documents (Bill of Lading, Master/Commercial invoice, packing list, customs export/import declarations), insurance certificates, axle-load and route engineering certificates, and payment milestone evidence such as signed delivery acceptance reports.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and export-control exposure: movement of heavy industrial plant components (e.g., turbines, pressure vessels, power generators) that could be diverted to restricted end-users or dual-use programs.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: End-user and end-use certificates from the final consignee, a copy of the freight forwarder's compliance due-diligence on restricted-party screening (UN, OFAC, EU, and PRC lists), a statement of no unsanctioned entities in the supply chain, and where applicable, an import/export license for the specific goods, fabricated in compliance with the PRC Export Control Law.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Under-capitalised WFOE with expected high transaction velocity relative to paid-in capital, triggering a source-of-funds review on domestic RMB operational accounts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A board-approved treasury forecast and cash-flow budget, the shareholders' loan agreement or future capital injection commitment, evidence of tax registration and historical VAT filings, and a notarised undertaking to provide monthly transaction declarations until the cumulative debit volume reaches the expected threshold.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Foreign investors make capital contributions by telegraphic transfer (SWIFT MT103) from the offshore shareholder account to the WFOE's Foreign Exchange Capital Account (FDI capital inflow) established at a SAFE-authorized bank. The bank must have received the FDI registration and a unique 'FDI-related business registration code' from SAFE prior to the receipt. The MT103 supplementary details should include the purpose code (e.g., 'investment registered capital' – PAYMENT OF SHARE CAPITAL) and the WFOE's Unified Social Credit Code. After arrival, the bank performs a transaction authenticity check, issues a capital account receipt confirmation, and the company files an FDI reinvestment/transaction report with SAFE. Under the settlement process, capital can be settled into RMB ('pay-as-you-go') based on the actual use under the Negative List; each RMB settlement must be backed by invoices/contracts with the counterparty.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For outbound payments related to project cargo logistics, the primary clearing rails are (i) SWIFT MT103 for milestone-based supplier and subcontractor payments in USD/EUR, requiring the service contract, commercial invoice, estimated BAF/CAF, and the bank's verification of the underlying 'real demand' to avoid 'orphan' flows; (ii) Commercial Letters of Credit (L/C) for heavy freight equipment procurement or when dealing with new suppliers who demand a bank undertaking; the WFOE may request an L/C from its CNY bank under the current account negative list or use a USD-backed L/C; (iii) Documentary Collections (D/P or D/A) for lower-risk trade settlements with established vendors. To reduce FX conversion friction and comply with SAFE, all RMB-denominated cross-border outbound payments can be routed via CIPS (Cross-Border Interbank Payment System), which enables same-day settlement and is increasingly accepted by Chinese logistics suppliers. Each transaction must be recorded with the correct BOP code (e.g., 222040 for freight transportation).
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Long-dated FX forward contracts (up to 12 months) for export/import payment hedging, subject to real-demand verification.
Cross-currency swaps for matched funding or trade-related cash flow swaps, approved by the bank's risk committee.
Bought FX options (call/put) to hedge contingent USD/CNY movements on bid bonds or milestone collections.
Cost-reduction structures such as collars or participating forwards are permitted only when the underlying trade flow is documented and the bank's compliance desk confirms no speculative intent.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Enterprise Annual Information Publicity Report (annual corporate return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) via the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 1 January to 30 June each year, reporting on the immediately preceding calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing after 30 June results in designation on the List of Enterprises with Abnormal Operations; failure to rectify for 3 consecutive years moves the company to the Serious Illegal and Untrustworthy Enterprise List, with government procurement restrictions, credit sanctions, and administrative deregistration risk; local SAMR enforcement may also impose fines.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) through the SAMR National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System (one-stop integrated reporting)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 1 January to 30 June each year, aligned with the SAMR annual report window
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: MOFCOM orders rectification within 20 days; failure to rectify attracts a fine of RMB 100,000 to 500,000 (about USD 14,000 to 70,000) under the Foreign Investment Law, plus credit-record consequences.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Enterprise Income Tax Annual Final Settlement Return (annual CIT filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) / local tax authority of the WFOE's registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 May of the year following the tax year (tax year is calendar year 1 January to 31 December)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing: penalty of up to RMB 2,000 (up to RMB 10,000 if serious) under the Tax Collection and Administration Law; overdue tax bears an interest-type surcharge of 0.05% per day; fraudulent under-declaration may trigger a penalty of 50% to 500% of the underpaid tax and possible criminal prosecution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Statutory Audit of Financial Statements (CPA audit report)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: No separate government filing; the audit report is retained at the registered office and furnished to SAMR, STA, or a lender/investor only when legally requested (e.g., SAMR random inspection or tax examination)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual financial reports for 31 December year-end must be prepared and audited before shareholder approval; practical filing deadline is before the 31 May CIT final settlement and before the 30 June annual report window
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to have the annual accounts audited as required by PRC Company Law creates regulatory liability for the company and its responsible officers, adverse findings in SAMR random annual-report checks, and weakened enforceability of shareholder claims; it does not directly trigger administrative strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No quantitative balance-sheet, turnover, or headcount threshold applies to this ordinary logistics WFOE. Under PRC Company Law, every limited liability company must prepare annual financial accounting reports and have them audited by a qualified PRC certified public accountant, irrespective of asset size, revenue, or employee count. Separate higher threshold-based audit regimes apply to listed issuers, banks, insurers, securities companies, trust/fund managers, and certain state-owned enterprises, none of which are triggered by this ISIC 5229 project cargo WFOE.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: PRC Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises (China GAAP), substantially converged with IFRS; eligible small enterprises may use the simplified Accounting Standards for Small Enterprises; income tax returns are reconciled to taxable income under the Enterprise Income Tax Law.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: PRC law does not impose a separate annual UBO declaration or public UBO register for a private WFOE. The WFOE must maintain a current register of shareholders and the SAMR annual report publicly identifies the equity holders and capital contribution status. Any equity transfer or change in controlling shareholder must be filed with SAMR within 30 days of the change; until registration, the change cannot be asserted against bona fide third parties. Banks and financial institutions may require beneficial-owner information for AML customer due diligence, and the foreign investment information annual report must identify the foreign investor and actual controller where relevant.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Shareholders (statutory register of members)
Resolutions and minutes of Board Meetings
Annual Financial Reports and CPA Audit Reports

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 600 to USD 2,000 per year for registered-office/secretarial agent services in a major mainland Chinese city
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,500 to USD 5,000 per year for a small-to-mid-sized WFOE with a simple capital structure

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general tax holiday for OOG logistics; possible reduced rate 15% for Encouraged High-Tech Enterprises if the WFOE engages in advanced logistics technology R&D (subject to certification), plus super-deduction of 100% for qualifying R&D expenses; small and low-profit enterprise preferential rate of 20% (actual effective at 5%/10% on first RMB 3 million if thresholds met) — non-resident-owned WFOE may elect if meeting conditions; additional preferential tax relief unavailable under specific free-zone regimes because the registered jurisdiction is Mainland China without special free-zone status.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: A200000 Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Class A), filed through China's State Taxation Administration e-Tax electronic filing system (e-tax.chinatax.gov.cn), with supplementary Form A107012 for related-party transactions and Form B100000 withholding declaration for non-resident payments.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; quarterly provisional CIT payments with preliminary returns due within 15 days after the end of each quarter, annual settlement return due before May 31 of the following calendar year.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a calendar-year fiscal year, the annual CIT return and self-assessment must be filed by May 31 of the following year; quarterly provisional declarations due April 15, July 15, October 15 and January 15 where applicable; monthly or quarterly WHT on non-resident income follows the deadline of 15 days after the month/quarter of the payment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross turnover from the supply of out-of-gauge heavy project cargo logistics services, including haulage, cranage, escort, freight forwarding, and marine/trailer subcontracting fees invoiced to clients in China and abroad.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Declare only Chinese-source revenue in this box in accordance with Article 6 of the EIT Law. If foreign-owned WFOE bills a non-resident parent or affiliate for logistics services, the amount must be consistent with the transfer-pricing documented arm's length price. Reclassify any offshore invoicing that shifts profit out of sight of the CIT return. Revenue from international transport (including project cargo from China to a third country) may be sourced to China under Article 7; the WFOE must apply the place of contract/operations management source rules and disclose any ambiguous cross-border deals as adjustments.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Costs of subcontracted heavy-haul trucking, barge/sea freight charter, port handling, oversized cargo permits, escort teams, stamp duties, insurance, and site preparation expenses directly attributable to revenue.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deduct only documented and business-related costs, with compliant VAT invoices for domestic costs. For costs paid to non-resident subcontractors, before deducting them you must confirm whether any payment constitutes service fee or royalty; if it is technically offshore service with no source in China, a WHT obligation still may arise under Article 3 if it is a service actually performed in China. If the cost is for intercompany royalty or interest paid offshore, it is subject to WHT and must be booked net; the deduction is allowed only if arm's length and substantiated.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciliation of accounting profit to taxable income: add back non-deductible fines, excess entertainment, imputed interest, and denied related-party costs; subtract tax-exempt government subsidies, previously taxed dividends from other resident enterprises, and CFC-subject adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Evaluate the transfer pricing adjustments under Public Notice [2016] No. 42: if the WFOE under-reported taxable income by mis-pricing OOG haulage charged to non-resident affiliates, this is the line where the undisputed adjustment is made pre-filing; failure to do so exposes the WFOE to a 10% penalty on the underpaid CIT (Public Notice [2017] No. 12 ineffective if voluntary adjustment is not documented). Mind the 5-year statute of limitation for adjustments, but fraud has no limitation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Offset of prior-year negative taxable income not older than 5 carrying years. The WFOE may use the remaining loss pool of its heavy-haul project logistics operations, limited to 5 years for general business losses, under Article 18 of the EIT Law.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident investors cannot deduct Chinese-source losses at the shareholder level. Ensure the loss carry-forward amount matches the last confirmed loss return; if a restructuring of a foreign parent occurred, the loss history may not be inherited unless it qualifies under continuity-of-business enterprise rules. Any change of ownership must be documented to avoid rejection.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 (Line 5 - Applicable Tax Rate and Tax Calculation)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statutory 25% headline rate applied to the taxable income; output tax for Chinese CIT; calculation of the quarterly provisional payments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the WFOE qualifies for reduced 15% preferential high-tech or Western Development zone treatment, attach the certificate; otherwise use 25%. No different rate applies to non-resident shareholders because WFOE is a resident. A non-resident investor must compute the 10% (or treaty-reduced) dividend WHT on the net dividend, not on the taxable income of the WFOE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credits for income taxes paid abroad on repatriated dividends or foreign branch income of the WFOE, capped at the Chinese CIT payable on that same foreign income under Article 23 of the EIT Law.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the WFOE receives intercompany service or transport fees in a foreign jurisdiction for which foreign taxes were withheld, include the foreign tax credit, but the excess must be carried forward 5 years. For non-resident investors the so-called deemed tax credit is unavailable for offshore payments; they are not filing this return, so any foreign tax is claimed separately in their home jurisdiction.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 7 (Line 7 - Withholding Tax Declaration on Non-Resident Payments)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of the China-source income paid or payable to non-resident enterprises (including foreign parent shareholders, lenders, licensors, and overseas subcontractors): outbound dividends, interest, rent, royalties, and transportation fees that have not borne Chinese tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This box requires bringing the non-resident payment into the WHT-return orbit. File with the annual filing the Report on the Approval of the Reduction or Exemption of Enterprise Income Tax for Non-Residents (Form A03053) for DTA benefits. Attach the non-resident's Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the treaty jurisdiction, evidence of beneficial ownership using the factors in SAT Announcement [2018] No. 9 (substance, risk, assets, and discretion), and the supporting agreement/service invoices. For a heavy haul project, payments to an overseas logistics intermediary may be considered China-source transportation if the transport takes place within Chinese territory; thus a 10% WHT (or treaty rate) must be withheld and paid to the tax authority by the 15th of the following month.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 8 (Line 8 - Quarterly Provisional Tax and Annual Balance)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of the final annual tax liability net of four quarterly provisional payments, including the amount due or the refund resulting from overpaid quarterly instalments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The annual settlement must reconcile the quarterly provisional balancing charge by May 31. For WFOE dividends to the non-resident parent, actual remittance is conditional on withholding and the payment of the WHT with a separate withholding return; if the shareholder is a Hong Kong investor entitled to 5% under the CN-HK DTA, obtain and attach a HK IRD residency certificate and a beneficial-ownership self-assessment to avoid re-imposition at the 10% rate.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the annual CIT return attracts a late-filing penalty of RMB 2,000 (or RMB 2,000-10,000 if aggravated) per return under Articles 32 and 62 of the Tax Collection and Administration Law (TCAL), plus a daily late-payment surcharge of 0.05% of the unpaid tax from the original due date. If the failure is associated with concealment of taxable income, the evasion penalty is 50%-500% of the evaded tax; if the evaded amount exceeds RMB 50,000 and is more than 10% of the tax due, a criminal case under Article 201 of the Criminal Law applies with liabilities against the utilising taxpayer and its officers. For non-resident WHT defaults, failure to withhold triggers a 50%-300% penalty against the withholding agent plus the criminal exposure.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: Effective statutory rate 10% on dividends distributed by a Chinese resident enterprise to a non-resident corporate shareholder (reduced from the 20% statutory rate by the EIT Law Article 27 implementation rules).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: A non-resident shareholder must submit, before each dividend distribution, a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the tax authority of the treaty jurisdiction, together with a written beneficial-ownership statement evidencing active business, substance, and not being a conduit using the factors of SAT Announcement [2018] No. 9. The withholding agent (WFOE) must apply the reduced rate under the applicable Double Tax Treaty (e.g. 5% under the China-Hong Kong DTA if the beneficial owner holds directly at least 25% of the shares of the WFOE for 12 months preceding the dividend). The application must be made via the non-resident tax withholding module on e-Tax before the payment is remitted, with supporting documentation kept on file. Refund of excess WHT should be requested under Article 4 of the treaty by filing a refund application with the county-level tax authority within three years.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory WHT on royalties for the use of patents, know-how, trademarks, and software in China is 10% (reduced from 20%) on the gross amount; statutory interest on intercompany loans paid to non-residents is also 10% (reduced from 20%) on the gross interest. Under the OECD-based China-Hong Kong DTA, interest and royalties are generally subject to 10% withholding; with certain treaties, royalty relief may be lowered to 5% for rentals of industrial or commercial equipment. The borrower/licensee must withhold at the statutory rate, then apply for treaty relief proportionally on the excess if the treaty rate is below the domestic rate.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: RMB 200 million for related-party tangible-goods transactions (such as the sale/purchase of heavy-haul equipment and project cargo materials), or RMB 40 million for service transactions (freight, haulage, subcontracting, management), royalties, and interest under SAT Public Notice [2016] No. 42; if neither threshold is crossed, a full Local File is optional but a Chinese CFC reporting form may still be required for related-party transactions exceeding RMB 25 million.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: While Mainland China has not enacted common-law Economic Substance Regulations (ESR), Article 47 of the EIT Law and Article 46 of the TCAL import the substance-over-form doctrine through the General Anti-Avoidance Rules (GAAR). The WFOE must demonstrate substantive decision-making, physical presence, employees, and revenue-generating assets in China in order to allocate logistics profit to the Chinese entity; a cross-border contract that merely routes legal title through a shell with no local management, staff, or assets will be re-characterised, causing adjustments to income and the denial of treaty benefits. The Core Income-Generating Activities (CIGA) of an OOG project cargo carrier must include dispatch, route planning, procurements and contract negotiation performed in China, and the WFOE should keep a contemporaneous functional-analysis file to support the allocated return.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE deliberately understates its taxable income by booking the heavy-haul project revenue of an out-of-gauge cargo movement as an intercompany cost-reimbursement to a Hong Kong affiliate, or by omitting milestone payments received from a foreign project client in an offshore bank account.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalty equal to 50%-500% of the evaded tax under Article 63 of the Tax Collection and Administration Law, plus a daily 0.05% late payment surcharge and a Criminal Law Article 201 offence if the evaded amount is above RMB 50,000 and over 10% of total tax payable.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The tax authority may pierce the corporate veil under Article 20 of the PRC Company Law, making directors jointly and severally liable to deliver assets to satisfy the tax arrears; the court may impose civil restitution of the evaded amount, freeze personal bank accounts, impose a travel ban (blacklisting limiting ability to leave China), and the responsible legal representative or CFO may face imprisonment for up to seven years, depending on the amount and aggravating circumstances.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the WFOE as a mere letter-box entity for a foreign parent: no board meeting in China, no actual dispatch or haulage management performed, no local employment, and all decision-making executed outside China, with profit artificially routed through Hong Kong.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 47 of the EIT Law and the General Anti-Avoidance Rules in SAT Public Notice [2016] No. 64, tax authorities can re-characterise the arrangement and impose CIT on income at the full 25%, require the withholding of 10% WHT on the deemed dividend, and assess a penalty of 50%-500% of the underpaid tax; the WFOE shall not receive crediting for any offshore tax in such case.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly signed the false substance declaration face personal civil liability to China's tax revenue, unlimited joint liability under the veil-piercing doctrine for the enterprise's tax debts, travel restrictions, and potential criminal liability for tax evasion under Article 201; if the shell is used for money laundering alongside the avoidance, the money-laundering offence under Article 191 of the Criminal Law could render the director liable to a sentence of 5-10 years in prison and seizure of personally held assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: False VAT Invoicing and Anti-Money Laundering (AML)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Issuing or obtaining fraudulent VAT special invoices for OOG project cargo services, such as inflated heavy-haul tonnage, fictitious oversized transport permits, or backdated subcontractor invoices, and then using these to claim VAT credits and administrative deductions, while routing proceeds through third-country shell accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The issuance of a false VAT invoice constitutes a criminal offence under Article 205 of the Criminal Law; penalties range from fines of 0.5-5 times the false-invoice amount, confiscation of property, and imprisonment for up to life imprisonment where the amount is extraordinarily large; additionally, the tax authority will refuse the deduction and impose a VAT penalty of 50%-500% under Article 63 of the TCAL.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A director that planned or endorsed the false-invoicing scheme is a co-principal offender, personally liable for the unpaid VAT and CIT plus fines; the court may strip the director's personal assets to compensate the tax administration, impose a travel ban until the penalty is paid, and imprison the director for 3-10 years (life in worst cases) for the tax fraud; any laundering of the resulting balance through cross-border transfers would also trigger Anti-Money-Laundering liability under Article 191, with the director subject to criminal confiscation and loss of director disqualification rights.
